title: Big Short Reunion w/ Danny Moses: Rising Rates, AI & Private Equity | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 80

metadata.title: Big Short Reunion w/ Danny Moses: Rising Rates, AI & Private Equity | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 80

summary: Danny Moses and Eisman examine higher rates, AI financing concentration, private-market incentives and fiscal risk. Moses favors diversified cash-generating technology on pullbacks but avoids weak neocloud balance sheets. Eisman stresses concentration and a long difficult period for leveraged PE. Both distinguish technological progress from investable returns. Moses's QE certainty and reserve concerns remain his own views, not Eisman predictions; Eisman emphasizes the lack of a comparable Treasury substitute.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Danny Moses supplies most cycle, private-credit and gold/QE claims. Eisman is separated where he adds the higher-for-longer, housing and concentration arguments.
framework_points: Compare financing structures and incentives across cycles.
Separate core franchise cash flow from marginal speculative capex.
Treat concentration and maturity mismatch as distinct risks.
Recognize short-selling timing and carry constraints.
transcript_cautions: A third-party strategist's S&P target is transcribed ambiguously as 6800 or 7800 and his rate forecast is repeatedly corrected; it is not treated as an Eisman prediction.
Nvidia receivables are subsequently described as revenue without substantiation.

claims.claim: Treasury's publicized long-bond buybacks are too small and predictable to overpower the bond market.

evidence.title: Treasury Announces Increased Sizes of Nominal Long-End Liquidity Support Buybacks
evidence.finding: The official stated purpose of larger long-end buybacks is liquidity support; the announcement doubles the per-operation maximum from $2 billion to at least $4 billion effective September 9.

claims.claim: Nvidia's reported concentration of 70% of receivables in five accounts shows major customer risk, which he then describes as 70% of revenue.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the original 10-Q and distinguish receivables concentration, direct customers and end customers.
claims.qualifications: The shift from accounts receivable to revenue is unsupported even if the receivables figure is correct.
claims.reason: The 70% receivables concentration is confirmed, but it cannot be relabeled as 70% of revenue. NVIDIA discloses revenue concentration separately, and the downstream labs are not identified by this receivables statistic.

evidence.title: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q
evidence.finding: Five customers represented 22%,14%,13%,11%,10% of receivables. This is not the revenue-concentration statistic; direct and indirect customer exposures are distinct.

claims.next_check: Inspect the original 10-Q and distinguish receivables concentration, direct customers and end customers.

claims.claim: The dollar remains dominant but its reserve share is around 57%, down substantially over decades; rising gold reserve value signals diversification pressure.
claims.speaker: Danny Moses
claims.test: Compare constant-price reserve quantities and consistent official-reserve denominators.
claims.reason: The current approximately 57% FX-reserve share is verified. Gold and Treasury portfolio shares use different denominators and valuation effects, so the broader replacement inference needs care.

evidence.title: COFER Q2 2026 Data Brief
evidence.finding: Dollar share of foreign-exchange reserves was 56.70%; dollar claims were broadly unchanged, while euro holdings increased. COFER excludes monetary gold.

claims.next_check: Compare constant-price reserve quantities and consistent official-reserve denominators.
